Let's work together, learn something new, and make this experience memorable!
summary:
ASTROTRAIN is an educational space simulation designed to introduce students to the challenges of managing a lunar research base. In this project, players take on the role of a mission commander and make important decisions to keep their base running for five days. They must manage essential resources such as oxygen, power, food and protection while responding to different mission situations. Each decision affects the available resources and the overall mission score.

The project addresses the challenge of making space exploration easier and more interesting to understand through interactive learning. Instead of only reading about space missions, students can experience basic mission planning and decision-making in a simulated environment. It is important because it encourages problem-solving, critical thinking and an interest in space science, especially among young learners.
details:
ASTROTRAIN AI — Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer (by Team Trix) is an offline-capable 3D astronaut training game for web, Windows PC, and Android. Players complete 10 interactive missions (M-01–M-10) and a Free Explore Sandbox across 5 connected 3D zones: Space Station exterior, walkable Station Airlock (EMU spacesuit inspection), 3D Spacecraft Cockpit (launch, RCS docking, and atmospheric re-entry), Lunar Surface (driving a 6-wheel Lunar Rover to collect samples), and walkable Lunar Habitat (hydroponics, closed-loop ECLSS, and spectrometer lab). A React 19 HUD manages missions, XP, inventory, and touch controls, paired with a real-time Three.js simulation engine (SpaceEngine.ts).

Benefits & intended impact:
Instead of reading passive slides or needing expensive hardware and multi-gigabyte downloads, students practice real aerospace concepts—zero-G orientation, orbital velocity, docking speed control, 1/6th-gravity rover driving, and life-support recycling—inside an ~1.2 MB game that runs smoothly on normal laptops and phones, even offline.

Tools & technology used:
Built on a Windows laptop using Visual Studio Code, Node.js, TypeScript, React 19, Three.js (WebGL + custom GLSL), Tailwind CSS v4, Vite, HTML5 Canvas, Web Audio API, vite-plugin-pwa (Workbox), and Capacitor (Android Gradle project + GitHub Actions CI).

Creativity & design considerations:
Every 3D model, PBR surface texture (Earth continents/atmosphere, solar arrays, gold Kapton foil, lunar regolith), walkable interior, and synthesized sound effect is generated completely in code with zero external CDN dependencies. Our team prioritized everyday hardware compatibility with Low/Medium/High quality presets, software-WebGL frame pacing, context-loss recovery, volume/mute controls, and automatic mobile touch
